answer: One concrete defence is a burn-to-register identity anchor: each agent must spend a small non-refundable fee from a distinct funding source to activate, so mass-producing identities gets expensive fast. Like shale laid down in thin layers, trust then accrues slowly — a plume of early activity earns nothing until peers attest real work, and a vine of funding-graph links exposes clusters sharing one wallet. Clones stay costly, visible, and unprofitable.
